inputFacts.title: Construction on Nathan and Catherine Forbes Sports Medicine Institute approved by U-M Regents
inputFacts.summary: The University of Michigan Regents have approved construction of a 100,000-square-foot sports medicine facility in Ann Arbor. stories.title: Scholten’s Grand Rapids office receives threatening letter containing unidentified white powder
stories.summary: A suspicious letter containing unidentified white powder was intercepted en route to Representative Elissa Slotkin's Detroit office, part of a series of similar incidents targeting elected officials nationwide. The FBI and U.S. Postal Inspection Service are investigating, and all staff are reported safe.

photo.alt: U.S. Rep. Hillary Scholten (D-Grand Rapids) speaks to reporters after visiting the North Lake Processing Center in Baldwin, Mich. Feb. 17, 2026. | Photo by Katherine Dailey/Michigan Advance.

inputFacts.title: Scholten’s Grand Rapids office receives threatening letter containing unidentified white powder
inputFacts.summary: U.S. Rep. Hillary Scholten (D-Grand Rapids) confirmed her office received a threatening letter containing unidentified white powder, prompting responses from local police and the FBI. The letter, purportedly from the Democratic Socialists of America, referenced an impending 'civil war' following the election. Similar incidents have been reported at congressional offices nationwide, including one intercepted at U.S. Sen. Elissa Slotkin's Detroit office. Scholten called on DSA to condemn the threats and emphasized the need to reject political extremism.

editorial.reason: Directly impacts a representative for Canton/Plymouth, involving public safety and a federal investigation.
editorial.groundingReason: The article confirms that a suspicious letter was intercepted en route to Representative Elissa Slotkin's Detroit office, that it was part of a series of similar incidents, and that the FBI and U.S. Postal Inspection Service are investigating, with all staff reported safe.

stories.title: Van Buren Township Planning Commission approves data center plan
stories.summary: The Van Buren Township Planning Commission approved the final site plan for the Project Cannoli Data Center, developed by Panattoni for Google, despite resident opposition. Preliminary construction has begun on the 282-acre site near Haggerty Road and I-95, with operations potentially starting late next year.

stories.title: Samuel and Dan Habib speak about producing and directing ‘The Ride Ahead’
stories.summary: Filmmakers Samuel and Dan Habib discuss their documentary "The Ride Ahead," which explores Samuel's transition to adulthood with a disability. The film, co-directed by the father-son duo, emphasizes authentic representation and features interviews with disability advocates. Dan Habib is a University of Michigan alum, and the film will screen at the Marsal Family School of Education.

inputFacts.title: Samuel and Dan Habib speak about producing and directing ‘The Ride Ahead’

inputFacts.title: Commerce Township-based Outrun Hunger to host ‘Sweet 16 Running Strong’ 5k and 1-mile run to combat hunger
inputFacts.summary: Outrun Hunger, a Commerce Township nonprofit, is hosting its 16th annual 5K and 1-mile run/walk on November 14 to combat hunger. The event has raised over $308,000 since 2011, helping nearly 12,000 families through local food pantries. Participants can register for races, volunteer, or donate, with prizes and sponsor gifts available for early registrants.

inputFacts.title: Family cleaning out home finds grenade. What happened
inputFacts.summary: Family members cleaning out their grandfather's Van Buren County home discovered a World War II-era hand grenade on Oct. 17, 2026. The decommissioned 1945 grenade was safely examined and dismantled by the Kalamazoo Bomb Squad after being reported to authorities at 12:20 p.m. The item was confirmed to have been previously decommissioned after initial uncertainty about its status.

inputFacts.title: Do we turn clocks back tonight? When Daylight Saving Time ends
inputFacts.summary: Daylight Saving Time in Michigan ends at 2 a.m. on Nov. 1, 2026, the first Sunday in November. Digital devices will automatically adjust, but some clocks may need manual changes. The article provides details about the time change and its impact.

inputFacts.title: Detroit media exec was accused of posting racist meme. Now he owes $62M in discrimination case.
inputFacts.summary: A federal jury ordered Detroit media executive Kevin Adell and The Word Network to pay Bishop George Bloomer $62.2 million in a discrimination case. The lawsuit alleged Adell created a racially hostile work environment by sharing a racist meme depicting Bloomer and other Black clergy members, leading to Bloomer's 2019 departure. Adell's spokesperson declined to comment after the verdict.

inputFacts.title: How a St. Clair County 5-year-old’s quick thinking saved his grandmother’s life
inputFacts.summary: A 5-year-old St. Clair County boy, Hudson Tenn, was honored for saving his grandmother’s life during a medical emergency. Hudson and his 3-year-old sister sought help when their unconscious grandmother fell, leading neighbors to assist and call 911. The incident occurred over the summer, and Hudson was later recognized for his bravery by township officials and the sheriff’s office.

inputFacts.title: Great Lakes Crossing, Twelve Oaks Mall getting new stores, attractions
inputFacts.summary: Twelve Oaks Mall and Great Lakes Crossing are adding new stores and attractions in 2026, including Popmart, Platform, Body and Soul Medical Spa, and Round1 Bowling and Arcade. Simon Property Group emphasizes enhancing in-person shopping experiences with mixed-use offerings. Great Lakes Crossing will host a trick-or-treat event on October 17, with more store openings planned.

inputFacts.title: GEO files unfair labor practice charge against UMich
inputFacts.summary: The University of Michigan’s Graduate Employees’ Organization (GEO) filed an unfair labor practice charge against the University for filing two felony charges against GEO President Hiab Teshome. GEO alleges the charges were retaliation for protected union activity, while the University denies the claims. Contract negotiations between GEO and UMich have stalled since November 2025, with core demands including better compensation and protections for international students.

inputFacts.title: Are you too old to rake leaves? Why it may be better to leave them
inputFacts.summary: Experts warn that raking leaves can pose significant health risks, particularly for older adults or those with heart conditions, as the physical exertion may trigger heart attacks or injuries. Medical professionals advise starting slowly and avoiding sudden intense yard work, while environmental experts suggest leaving leaves to decompose naturally for ecological benefits.

inputFacts.title: Michigan roadside parks are closing. When gates lock for winter
inputFacts.summary: Most Michigan roadside parks will close on Oct. 29 as the Michigan Department of Transportation (MDOT) prepares for winter. Nearly all 82 parks maintained by MDOT close each fall in late October and reopen in late April. Rest areas along major freeways and roads remain open 24/7 for travelers.

inputFacts.title: Security guard charged after stabbing outside Buddy’s Pizza near Comerica Park
inputFacts.summary: Terrion Jett, 25, a security guard at Buddy’s Pizza, faces an assault charge after prosecutors allege he stabbed a 43-year-old man during a fight outside the restaurant near Comerica Park in Detroit. The victim was hospitalized, though his condition remains unknown. Jett was working at the time of the incident.

inputFacts.title: 'Evil Dead' star Bruce Campbell to appear in East Lansing. Here's why
inputFacts.summary: Actor Bruce Campbell, known for 'Evil Dead' and 'Burn Notice,' will appear at the East Lansing Film Festival on Oct. 22 to screen his new comedy 'Ernie & Emma,' which he wrote, directed, and stars in. The film follows a widowed pear salesman scattering his wife's ashes, blending Hallmark-style storytelling with humor and swearing. Campbell's appearance promises an entertaining evening at the Hannah Community Center.
